_what: This is the not-done contrast arm (gold_coverage_v2 export) trained with --exclude-decided-by stop_done.
_not_here_on_purpose: base_model and adapter. Under reference=adapter the policy IS rung 1's LoRA, so the adapter path is the run's identity and must be typed, not defaulted.
_why_max_seq_len: MEASURED on the real tokenizer: the longest state is 4,963 tokens and the longest templated example ~5,045. 5,120 is the next multiple of 1,024 above that.
_why_max_prompt_len: 512 below max_seq_len, which is well above the longest action (a question is 40-120 characters). On trl 1.x there is no separate prompt budget at all and this is recorded rather than applied -- `prompt_length_hook` in rung2.manifest.json says which regime the run was under, because truncating the prompt and truncating the concatenation are not the same experiment.
_why_bf16: As rung 1: the compute dtype, not a storage dtype.
_why_batch_and_accum: As rung 1. Two forward passes per example here, so the wall time per step is roughly twice rung 1's.
_why_learning_rate: 5e-6, an order of magnitude below rung 1: DPO moves a policy that already exists.
_why_epochs: One pass. A preference dataset re-visited is a preference dataset memorised.
_why_beta: 0.1 is the standard DPO KL weight. It is in cfg.sha because beta and label_smoothing are the two fields that define the objective itself.
_why_loss_type: Plain DPO -- the default, named here because the objective is the one thing this grid should never leave implicit. A single name renders in cfg.sha as the bare string the pre-tuple field rendered, so writing it changes nothing about this run's identity. `["sigmoid", "sft"]` with loss_weights is the RPO/MPO arm; it is a second run, not an edit of this one.
_why_include_pair_kinds: This is the not-done contrast arm (gold_coverage_v2 export) trained with --exclude-decided-by stop_done, restricted to the synthesised not-done stop pairs alone.
_why_reference: The frozen rung-1 adapter, not a merge: a bf16 fold lost 44.7% of rung 1's update and the fp32 fix makes an 8B base ~32 GB that this rung would then load. See docs/TRAINING.md 6.1.
